options.blogdescription: Adds Open Graph metadata to your pages

steps.code:
1, 'post_title' => 'How to check the Open Graph metadata', 'post_name' => 'open-graph', 'post_excerpt' => 'The Open Graph plugin has no settings page. Open the source code of this page to see the metadata.', 'post_content' => '

The Open Graph plugin has no settings page. It works out of the box and adds Open Graph metadata to the <head> of your posts and pages.

You can not see the metadata on the page itself. To check it, open the source code of this page and search for og:. You should find tags like og:title, og:description, og:url and og:type.

In Playground the site runs inside a frame, so use right click and "View Frame Source" (Chrome) or "This Frame" → "View Frame Source" (Firefox). "View Page Source" only shows the Playground app itself.

Try to edit this post, change the title or add a featured image, and check the source again. The plugin uses the featured image (or the images in the post) for og:image.

If you want to change the output, you can use the opengraph_metadata filter, or a filter per property like opengraph_title or opengraph_image.
